originals.inspection: Individually inspected2012 full north facade: square tall tower, low two hanging corner bartizans and four top corner turrets; three stacked window registers with central ornate twin-arched balcony and upper paired opening; deep machicolated walk, shield merlons, recessed upper terrace, beaded finials and low tide foundation exposed. Bridge appears to left/east; no people/boats reproduced.

originals.inspection: Individually inspected2006 court/terrace: actual lower open rectangular courtyard, pointed door openings, quatrefoil pierced parapet, tall pinnacles and domed bastion turrets beyond. Open court cannot be replaced with solid full-height base.

coverageGaps: Bridge route/width/supports and ornaments are conservative photographic estimates. No measured construction drawing.

primarySources.review: Tower and broad artillery bastion distinct; four vaulted tower rooms. Manueline nautical ropes, armillary spheres, crosses and naturalistic motifs.

Four-storey tower and polygonal bastion,16 low artillery embrasures, shield merlons and open cloister/courtyard. Browser inspection of the full south-facade photograph confirms a long open arcaded loggia below two separate arched balconied windows with central royal shield, plus Madonna canopy and pierced lower court railings. This south facade differs materially from the north twin arcade. West bastion photograph shows low rectangular artillery openings, projecting corner turrets and open terrace/court. South aerial constrains the L-shaped elevated approach and shore retention basin. No measured drawing or tidal survey claim.
